claims.text: Laser powder-bed fusion with a controlled scanning strategy and optimized process parameters can improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed intervention reduces compositional segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed intervention reduces residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed intervention limits defect formation in AlCrFeNiSi.
A laser power of 200 W, scanning speed of 500 mm/s, layer thickness of 50 μm, and preheating temperature of 200°C constitute suitable processing conditions for the intervention.
The intervention produces a refined AlCrFeNiSi microstructure with reduced segregation and porosity.
Controlled scanning and optimized process parameters reduce thermal gradients and stresses.
Reduced thermal gradients and stresses promote a more homogeneous microstructure.
Reduced thermal gradients and stresses limit defect formation.
The intervention increases yield strength by 15% relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention reduces porosity by 20% relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
The hypothesis is valid for AlCrFeNiSi powder processed by laser powder-bed fusion under conditions similar to those specified.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a 15% yield-strength increase and 20% porosity reduction, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 10% and 15%, respectively. Thus, results can fall short of both quantitative predictions without falsifying the hypothesis.
